title: Formal Methods Tool Accessibility Benchmark: Can Novice CS Students Use Lean 4 with AI Assistance?

original_idea.body:
# Formal Methods Tool Accessibility Benchmark: Can Novice CS Students Use Lean 4 with AI Assistance?

**Problem:** A key constraint in this subfield: Lean 4 expertise is rare and the learning curve is steep. Whether CS students with only basic Python and CS fundamentals can productively use AI-assisted Lean 4 verification tools (Leanstral, VSCode Lean plugin + Claude) is unknown.

**Direction:** Recruit 15 CS students (intro-level). Give them 4 hours to solve 5 Lean 4 programming problems using AI assistance (Leanstral + Claude). Measure: problems solved, time per problem, number of compiler error loops, subjective difficulty rating. Compare to 0% vs. expert baseline.

**Why it matters:** If novice CS students can solve basic Lean 4 problems with AI assistance, formal verification can be democratized. If not, AI tools remain gated by Lean expertise, preventing the broad adoption the RAND vision requires.

**Relevant context:** RAND (2026) calls for broad adoption of formal methods. Current tools are expert-oriented. The VeriBench paper notes that even sophisticated models struggle; a user study of novice+AI is missing.
